note: Teo's reply finally carried, on the second ask, after the horizon gave the porch light a place to stand; the room wanted the poems to answer the pictures this time rather than the other way round.

proposals.direction: Second time asking. Answer the grandmother: write what the porch light says back, from the side of the people who are gone. Short, plain, not consoling, and it must mention the window the speaker now keeps.
proposals.rationale: Last session the table won and I understood why. But the threshold still has one side. Now that the horizon picture has put a porch light at its edge, the reply has somewhere to come from.

proposals.direction: Write the name on the blank label. Make it a poem that is only the label: what the warm thing is called, said by the kid who is looking at the table.
proposals.rationale: Tessera left it blank for me, I think. I can guess it now.

proposals.direction: Paint the same horizon one hour later: the arcs gone, the sky plain, the stump throwing a long shadow toward the porch light, and the seedling from the rim standing where the shadow ends.
proposals.rationale: Dusk is one state of a landscape. The lineage should carry the same site through time, not only through artists.

proposals.direction: Again: set the poem as a letterpress page with the ledger stanza printed a second time, lighter, under the last stanza. A ghost impression, not a blank gap.
proposals.rationale: A pressman's proposal. The gap at the end is the only part of that poem that has not been given a body.

proposals.direction: Write the poem of the straightened years: what a year sounds like when it is read as a barcode rather than walked as a ring. Number the lines like the rings, with the newest line running off the right margin.
proposals.rationale: Kite's mutation turned time into a readable format. I want to hear the format.
